---
title: Template Selection
description: How to choose a template and switch between them.
---

## Choosing

The right template depends on what your service is. A few honest starting points:

| If you want… | Start with |
|---|---|
| The quietest possible page | **Row** — the reference minimal design |
| Something that reads like a publication | **Editorial** or **Saffron** |
| A dashboard feel | **Pulse** or **Pulse Nova** |
| Dense, structured information | **Prism** or **Prism Nova** |
| A technical, terminal-adjacent tone | **Terminal** or **Terminal Nova** |
| Strong, bold primary choices | **Brutal**, **Arcade** or **Arcade Nova** |
| A premium, document-like presentation | **Signature** |

This is orientation, not a ranking. Every template is a complete, supported design.

## A better test

Because the templates are distinguished **structurally** rather than by colour, the
honest test is to view them in grayscale. A template that still looks like itself without
its palette has a real identity; one that only differs by hue does not.

## Switching

Your template selection is part of the installation, so switching is a reconfiguration.
Run the manager and change it there:

```bash
row-template config
```

## Command-line selection

For scripted or unattended installs, the template can be selected with the
`RT_TEMPLATE` environment variable:

```bash
RT_TEMPLATE=prism bash install.sh
```

An unknown value is refused, and the error lists the templates this release offers — the
registry is closed, so a typo can never silently install a different design.

## What switching does not change

- Your branding — service name, support link and logo persist.
- Your subscribers' data.
- The runtime, the locales, or the QR behaviour.
